Missing a payment does not lead to disconnection right away. Accounts more than 45 days past due are flagged for a service review, and the disconnection policy applies only to non-payment exceeding 90 days [Billing & Account FAQs > What happens if I miss a payment?].

If your miss came from a failed autopay charge:

- SunGrid retries the charge twice more over the following 5 business days. If those retries fail, the account is treated as manual-pay for that billing cycle [Autopay Failure & Retry Policy > What Happens When Autopay Fails?].
- You'll be notified by email and in the member portal after the first failed attempt, with instructions to update your payment method. A second notification is sent if the retry also fails [Autopay Failure & Retry Policy > Notifications].
- The 45-day and 90-day timelines are counted from the original due date, not from the date autopay failed [Autopay Failure & Retry Policy > Relationship to Late Payment Policy].
- You can re-enroll in autopay at any time under Account Settings in the member portal. Re-enrollment takes effect on the next billing cycle [Autopay Failure & Retry Policy > Re-Enrolling in Autopay].

The excerpts also say community-tier members are not disconnected from shared array access over billing disputes. They don't say how that applies to other billing situations. For questions about your specific account or balance, please contact SunGrid member support.

System size and income are hard requirements. A household that fails either one gets no rebate, regardless of how it scores on the other rules [Incentive & Rebate Programs > Rooftop Rebate Program].
